newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Forests year profit seen falling.
newsitem.headline: FCL Forests year profit seen falling.

text.p: Low log prices are expected to erode Fletcher Forests annual earnings, before abnormals, to around NZ$60-65 million when it posts its annual result on Wednesday.

That would compare with NZ$74 million in the year to June, 1996. But analysts expect significant abnormal items of around NZ$85 million, in the form of surpluses from the sale of Hikorangi forest on the East Coast, the share of some Nelson forests and the sale of the South Auckland forest estate.
Low log prices were expected to make their presence felt, as were higher operating costs in the second half.
Costs in the first half were lower because the harvest took place closer to mills and ports. In the second half, the forests were further away and more expensive to harvest.
Furthermore, FCL Forests shifted away from its own estate to that of the partnership which bought Kaingaroa State Forest, in which the company has a 37.7 perent stake.

David Stanley, forestry analyst at Doyle Paterson Brown, said a decline in Douglas fir prices over the second half coincided with a slowing of the Japanese housing market and a strong New Zealand dollar.
But the market's focus had already shifted to the current financial year, when analysts expect to see the benefits derived from the buy-in to the Forestry Corp assets.
